items.title: Bounty auto earner: one click delivery packager for the six proven report services
items.body:
Owner directive 2026-10-23 evening: build BOTH earning programs toward the 1 dollar per minute target. This task is the bounty lane half, repo work only.

Goal: cut the delivery time for a won 10 USD report job to under 10 minutes of compute, start to checked deliverable, so a delivered job earns at or above 1 dollar per minute while it runs.

Build, inside this repo only:
1. A delivery packager that takes a job spec (service name, subject, buyer ask) for the six proven services (recall, FMCSA carrier, federal litigation, Form D, nonprofit, federal awards) and assembles the report from the existing fetchers in tools/ and the templates in workstream D, with every claim carrying its source and retrieval time.
2. A verification pass that fails the package if any claim lacks a source, if counts do not match the fetcher output, or if the deliverable hash is not recorded.
3. A timing log per delivery run, so the coordinator can report minutes per job and dollars per minute honestly.
4. One filled example per service, built from public data only, checked the same way.

Rules: repo work only. No bids, no submissions, no accounts, no keys, no wallet or payment handling in this repo; bidding and delivery on Synmerco, NEAR, and the other lanes stay with the coordinator and the existing lane jobs under their standing approvals. No pricing changes in this task; pricing is the owner decision and is tracked on issue 147.

Acceptance: packager runs on all six services, verification pass demonstrably fails a deliberately unsourced example, timing log exists, and the PR states the measured minutes per example job.

items.title: Add Bug Bounty Intelligence (provider, MCP server and security scanner on Base)
items.body:
Adds Bug Bounty Intelligence as a provider with two Base listings, submitted by the project owner. It replaces #4746, which a community contributor opened and then closed so the owner could submit this one.

- Provider: Bug Bounty Intelligence, repository github.com/holistis/bug-bounty-intelligence-mcp, contact info@tokenizen.nl.
- mcpservers: bug-bounty-intelligence-mcp. MCP server, run with npx -y bug-bounty-intelligence-mcp@latest (published on npm, version 1.0.3). Free pattern search. A full-repo scan costs 5 USDC on Base through x402.
- security: al-mizaan-solidity-scan. The same service as a hosted scanner. The payment address is 0x015Eb036560216B3051339061FF68A207E0fe88f, the one in the repository README and in the live payment request at https://x402.tokenizen.nl/api/bug-intel.
- The logo is a simple mark we drew, 400 by 400 px, transparent background.

The claims in the descriptions come from the README. Column counts match the headers in all five files.

items.title: S23: add local market escrow, delivery and bounties
items.body:
Closes #23.

Blacksite now supports local player listings, banked bid escrow, net buyout settlement, exact-instance protected delivery and anonymous local bounties paid by normal contested/open-zone deaths. Money, item ownership, delivery, Kestrel fees, market records and private audit commit through one commerce source. Schema 4 preserves bid/history snapshots, expiry and retirement refunds.

Public-terminal F9 services preserve E contract-board interactions and street M/O/C map/drone/chat. Market D bids, Esc/B leaves, and Y confirms a chosen transfer. Purchased goods collect free from market-tagged delivery; unsold returns restore inventory weight so cancellation cannot bypass apartment storage. Views and operator list responses are paged for accumulated history. S28/S29/S30 and S25 handoffs retain PR #38 and issue #56 decisions.

Validation:
- Full root pytest at f23120938ec42af75d8853337ef839dc5304218b: Linux/Python 3.12 1,449 passed; Windows/Python 3.12 1,448 passed, one skipped (last Windows gate green; detailed final log will be recorded).
- Latest local UI: 11 passed at fake 80x24/132x50 with wide names, including actual Display.key hotkeys. Protocol/atomicity/effective-carry: 9 passed.
- Native acceptance is NOT complete. Installed 0.0.19 through actual NetBBS 7.31 native stdio at 80x24 reaches public services and lists the physical starter pistol. That exposed missing advertised action metadata, now fixed and covered through the real client key model. A subsequent buyer route hit an unexpected chat prompt; its failed trace is retained and under investigation. The parallel 132x50 attempt timed out during cold door launch before gameplay.
- Matching wheel SHA256 c7cf366a02bfa5c1dd2dc4c1788b65ef54876bb892f653fb98e611d5f8787a2f; full Python tree 648ed4b004bed7aa2e5007454f24039941659d5d5b9bd8a94d77c65b77c5faaf. Actual native success, independent persisted-state checks, final-head CI and written review remain merge gates.

Design changes: game 8.3 clarifies whole-chit ceiling for the existing 5% fee, own-bid credit toward buyout, exact free purchased delivery and unsold inventory return. Entity 2.6, architecture 15.2 and terminal UI 4 describe records, atomicity, access and bounded views. S23 uses actual commissioned Vatside contested geography; S25 retains actual Sink travel and real commerce/clinic acceptance, and S25/S26 retain human pacing gates. Grade/full-pool/bank fixtures are disclosed; no item, placement, reward or future-map fixture is used.

Preferred slice implementer: Sonnet. Actual implementer: Codex (GPT-6); automated Claude review supplies the review gate. Triage will fix credible caller/operator/security/data-loss impact and explain deferrals of theoretical correctness findings.

items.title: [Bounty proposal] fix(retrieval): harden result_bounds edge cases and apply context bounding to omi_tools ( proposed)
items.body:
### Summary
In retrieval tools, `result_bounds.py` and `omi_tools.py` contained several edge-case crash and context-overflow vulnerabilities:

1. **Negative `max_items` Slicing**: In `cap_items_for_llm`, when `max_items < 0` (e.g. computed limits after offset), Python sliced from the end `items[:max_items]` (e.g. `items[:-1]` dropped 1 item instead of returning empty list). Now returns `[], total_found, total_found > 0`.
2. **`None` / Non-string TypeError in `bounded_result`**: Calling `bounded_result(None)` raised unhandled `TypeError: object of type 'NoneType' has no len()`. Coerced defensively to safe string representation.
3. **Negative `shown` Normalization**: Clamped `shown_count = max(0, shown)` to prevent negative count annotations.
4. **Context Overflow in `omi_tools.py`**: `get_omi_product_info_tool` accumulated arbitrary numbers of documentation markdown files without applying `bounded_result`, risking context window overflow and model freezing (issue #4927). Now bounded to `MAX_RESULT_CHARS` (60,000 chars) with truncation guidance.
5. **Query Validation & Non-Dict Resilience**: Supports optional/None queries with structured error response instead of crashing, and verifies `context` is a valid mapping before invoking `.items()`.

### Unit Test Verification
All 20 tests pass hermetically across both test suites:
```
python -m pytest backend/tests/unit/test_retrieval_result_bounds.py backend/tests/unit/test_omi_tools_resilience.py -v
======================== 20 passed, 1 warning in 2.55s ========================
```

### Proposed Bounty
- **Proposed Reward**: $50 USD on merge
- **Preferred Payout**: Algora / Crypto
- **Contributor**: @MD-Mushfiqur123

items.title: Add bug bounty + mobile API skills, a practice lab, and skill corpus tests
items.body:
## Why

Three gaps surfaced while using Strix for bounty-style web/API work:

1. **No bounty-program workflow skill.** `api_spec_testing` covers a contract but
   not the things that decide whether a run pays: scope/authorization gates,
   duplicate economics, impact chaining, and what triage will accept.
2. **No mobile skill at all.** The most valuable target behind an app is its API,
   but nothing in the library stops an agent from asserting device-level results
   (decompilation, pinning bypass, runtime hooking) it cannot produce — the
   sandbox has no `adb`, `frida`, `jadx`, `apktool`, or MobSF.
3. **No practice target and no guardrails on the skill corpus itself.**

## What changed

### Skills (`strix/skills/custom/`)

| Skill | Coverage |
| --- | --- |
| `bug_bounty_programs` | Preconditions, automation policy, duplicate economics table, surface prioritisation (version drift, undocumented siblings), impact chaining, triage-proof report shape, budget control |
| `authorization_matrix` | Actor × object × verb matrix, object-id enumeration sources, where the check is usually missing, bypass techniques, six-point false-positive gate, severity mapping, coverage ledger |
| `mobile_api_testing` | Input contract (traffic/spec/source/static artefacts), endpoint normalisation, mobile-specific priority order (BOLA, client-supplied trust headers, token lifecycle, OTP/device binding, deep links, attestation gaps), validation rules, report fields |

### Practice lab (`labs/vulnerable-api/`)

A single-file, standard-library-only API with nine planted bugs — BOLA, BFLA,
mass assignment to admin, JWT `alg:none`, excessive data exposure, SQLi, OTP
brute force, negative-amount business logic, unsalted MD5 storage. Ships a
bundled OpenAPI contract (so `-t ./openapi.json` works out of the box), seeded
accounts, reset/OTP helper endpoints, and `find_bugs.sh` for reference.

`make lab` starts it on loopback. Bandit excludes `labs` and ruff has scoped
per-file ignores, with comments, because the vulnerabilities are deliberate.

### Tests

- `tests/test_skills_corpus.py` — frontmatter parses, `name` matches the file,
  description/body non-empty, unique bare names, and the three new skills load
  with their expected sections. This is the first guardrail on the skill corpus.
- `tests/test_vulnerable_api_lab.py` — asserts every planted weakness is still
  exploitable, so the lab cannot be silently "fixed" out of usefulness.

### Docs

New pages: **Bug Bounty Workflow**, **Mobile App Testing**, **Practice Lab**
(added to `docs/docs.json`). New skills listed in `docs/advanced/skills.mdx` and
`strix/skills/README.md`. `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` point contributors at
the lab and the corpus test.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/test_vulnerable_api_lab.py tests/test_skills_corpus.py` → 173 passed
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean on every added file
- `mypy --strict` clean on the added test modules
- `find_bugs.sh` reproduces all nine findings against a live instance
- Skill discoverability confirmed via `get_available_skills()`
